comment: Third-party components aember can put on a device. doc/licensing/THIRD_PARTY.md explains it; `aember pack` writes the notices of the ones present (aember-cli/aember/steps/packaging/notices.py). detect: globs relative to the image root ('*' = always); packages: Yocto package names from an opt-in package's packages.txt.

components.name: aember (init, aember-netd, aember-containerd)
components.obligation: our own licence (LICENSE)

components.name: Linux kernel
components.linking: separate program (user space talks to it through system calls)
components.obligation: source offer (GPL/LGPL): the exact source, our patches and build config, for 3 years (incl. aember-resources' kernel config fragments)

components.name: BusyBox
components.obligation: source offer (GPL/LGPL): the exact source, our patches and build config, for 3 years (incl. the .config)

components.name: GNU C Library (glibc variants)
components.obligation: source offer (GPL/LGPL): the exact source, our patches and build config, for 3 years; users may replace the library (dynamic linking does that)

components.name: musl libc (-musl variants)
components.obligation: keep the copyright notice (NOTICES)

components.name: GCC runtime: libstdc++, libgcc_s
components.linking: dynamic; the GCC Runtime Library Exception lets non-GPL programs use it
components.obligation: none beyond the notice, as long as we compile with an unmodified GCC (the exception's 'Eligible Compilation Process')

components.obligation: source offer (GPL/LGPL): the exact source, our patches and build config, for 3 years; our patch is part of it; users may replace the library
